headline_marked: [[vLLM Semantic Router]] silently dropped requests due to blocking CPU-bound tasks
headline: vLLM Semantic Router silently dropped requests due to blocking CPU-bound tasks
summary: A developer shares how a traffic spike exposed a critical flaw in their vLLM semantic router setup, leading to silent request failures and a dramatic increase in latency.
details: A developer experienced a critical issue where their FastAPI gateway, which wraps the vLLM semantic router, began silently dropping requests during a 2 AM traffic spike. Instead of errors, Prometheus showed route decision latency skyrocketing from 80ms to 4.8 seconds, after which requests simply vanished from logs.

The root cause was identified as the synchronous embedding computation within the semantic-router library, which was blocking the asyncio event loop. While it performed well under local load testing, production traffic patterns with bursts of over 300 concurrent requests overwhelmed the synchronous CPU-bound tasks, causing requests to be silently discarded after an internal 5-second timeout.

The solution involved moving the blocking embedding computation off the main event loop using `asyncio.to_thread()`. This delegates the CPU-bound work to a thread pool, freeing the asyncio event loop to accept new requests and preventing head-of-line blocking.

After implementing the thread pool fix, P95 routing latency dropped dramatically from 4800ms to 320ms under the same load conditions, with zero dropped requests. The team now enforces a rule: any library using synchronous model inference must be offloaded to threads or a separate process pool when called from async handlers.

The most concerning aspect was the silent failure mode, where requests timed out and disappeared without any explicit error codes. The developer stresses the importance of emitting explicit timeout metrics and tracing request lifecycles end-to-end when debugging async bottlenecks to avoid such issues.

headline_marked: Anthropic launches [[Claude Duet]], an AI assistant that proactively manages tasks
headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, an AI assistant that proactively manages tasks
summary: The new AI agent aims to streamline workflows by handling emails, calendars, and app interactions.
details: Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a new AI assistant designed to proactively manage tasks across various connected applications. This move positions Anthropic to compete with similar AI agents from companies like OpenAI and Meta.

Claude Duet is capable of keeping track of emails and calendars, and can reportedly interact with other apps to complete tasks. This functionality aims to reduce the manual effort required for everyday digital management.

The introduction of Claude Duet signifies a growing trend in AI development towards more integrated and proactive personal assistants. These agents are expected to become increasingly sophisticated in handling complex workflows.

While specific details on its availability and integration capabilities are still emerging, Claude Duet represents Anthropic's commitment to advancing AI beyond simple conversational models into practical task management tools.
